● Colin's component renders fine under node, so the white square must be

● Reproduced in Chromium: Colin's SFC is parsed but its injections never commit,
  so the widget is never constructed — the white square. Digging into why.

  Searched for 1 pattern, ran 3 shell commands (ctrl+o to expand)

● Found the deadlock: a newly pasted SFC layer only gets injected when a
  component requests it, but InfusionHost waits for the layer definition first.
  I'll fix this by having fluid.ptf.registerLayerPart bind the freshly
  registered SFC into the default document, mirroring what <fluid-import> does.

● Update(src/framework/core/js/FluidPTF.js)

● Found the root cause: array mutation methods on the proxy write to a separate
  live signal at state.entries, bypassing $reactiveRoot at state, which leaves
  liveLayer.state as a plain object and triggers the existing.set is not a 
  function error later. I'll fix this by routing those mutations through
  fluid.setForComponent.

● No lint errors in any touched file. Checking whether the AI's prompt material
  documents the limitations I've just fixed.

  Searched for 2 patterns, ran 1 shell command (ctrl+o to expand)

● I've fixed both issues and everything in the #24 checklist. npm test passes
  1345/1345 (1307 before, plus new regression tests), and fluid-lint-all reports
  nothing in the files I changed. I also ran the tldraw demo in Chromium to
  check the paste, copy and markdown behaviour. Nothing is committed and dist/,
  docs/ and the .mjs builds haven't been regenerated, so npm run build is still
  needed.

  #23 – copying text from the "Ask me anything" transcript
  tldraw listens for copy at the document level, and stays focused while you
  click in the panel. So any copy made while a shape was selected copied the
  canvas selection instead of your text. A new guardClipboardEvents in
  tldraw-clipboard.js stops copy and cut events from the panel before they reach
  tldraw. In Chromium, a copy from the panel no longer gets taken over, while a
  copy on the canvas still is.

  #24 – framework fixes
  1. $if going false left the child's content on the page. The existing test
     only passed because its child template was empty. A view with no template
     of its own now renders the placeholder markup from its parent's template,
     so the content is cleared. I added content to that test so it covers this
     case.
  2. Arrays inside a $reactiveRoot. Mutating methods like push wrote to a
     separate path, bypassing the reactive root. That lost the write and caused
     the later existing.set is not a function. They now go through
     fluid.setForComponent. Reassigning a spread ([...state.entries, x]) also
     overflowed the stack, because the proxies in the new array were written
     back; they are now unwrapped. The new test fails with exactly the reported
     symptoms on the old code.
  3. fluid.filterKeys no longer uses jQuery; it's built on fluid.filterObjKeys,
     which moved into Fluid.js. I also removed a second $.extend in
     fluid.parsePriorityRecords.
  4. fluid.formatUnavailable now exists. The unavailable proxy's
     Symbol.toPrimitive was also broken (String(proxy) threw), and both now go
     through the new function.

  #24 – panel and paste items
  - Colin's component: its file is fine. The cause was a deadlock. A pasted SFC
    layer that the page didn't already have was only set up once a component
    asked for it, but the demo waited for the layer before creating anything.
    Registering a layer from a PTF document now sets it up straight away, and
    his cat pastes and renders correctly.
  - Diagnostics for failed pastes:
    - A malformed document is reported in the panel as a formatting problem, and
      nothing is pasted from it.
    - A widget that can't be built is reported in the panel as an instantiation
      problem.
    - A shape that is still blank after 8 seconds now shows what went wrong
      instead of a white square. It only does this when the shape has rendered
      nothing, so a widget that is slowly loading is left alone.
  - More forgiving parsing: anything before the first MIME-Version: 1.0 is now
    ignored.
  - Plain-text pastes that aren't PTF go into the Ask box. Only clipboards
    holding plain text alone are routed there, since tldraw's own copies always
    include HTML and must still paste as shapes. One consequence: a URL copied
    as plain text now goes to the Ask box rather than becoming a bookmark.
  - Model field is now read-only, and the remembered model setting is gone,
    since it could no longer be changed.
  - Markdown: I added snarkdown 2.0.0 (about 1 KB, MIT) under
    src/lib/snarkdown/. The AI's replies are rendered through it; your own
    messages, errors and change notes stay plain text. Text is escaped first and
    only http(s) links and images are kept, because snarkdown passes raw HTML
    straight through.
  - Conversation entries now live inside state, which works now that nested
    arrays are fixed.

  Two things I noticed but left alone: JSON.stringify on a proxied array still
  throws, and Colin's PTF records the auto-changer as on even though its timer
  isn't restored after the paste.

● Looks right. Full suite and lint:

  Ran 1 shell command (ctrl+o to expand)

● The image widget now finds a matching photo on Pixabay and shows it with its
  credit, and every request to IFM gets a metrics line in the "Ask me anything"
  transcript. npm test passes 1364/1364 and lint is clean on the changed files.
  I also checked both in Chromium against the live Pixabay API; the IFM metrics
  there used a stubbed reply.

  Image widget
  - Search: "Find Image" searches Pixabay for the prompt (trimmed to the API's
    100-character limit, with SafeSearch on). "Another" steps through the other
    results.
  - Credit: the image is shown inside the widget with "Image by contributor from
    Pixabay", linking to the contributor's profile and the image's page. This
    is the format Pixabay asks for.
  - Change in behaviour: the old widget dropped a dashed placeholder onto the
    canvas. The new one doesn't put the image on the canvas. Pixabay's image
    links expire after 24 hours and its terms don't allow storing them
    permanently, which putting them on the canvas would do.
  - Pixabay's terms: results are cached for 24 hours as the terms require. If a
    widget pasted from an old PTF document shows an expired image, it looks the
    image up again once to get a fresh link.
  - The key: the browser reads it from pixabay-api-key.txt at the repo root.
    That file wasn't gitignored, so I added it to .gitignore. Anyone who opens
    the demo page can see the key, because the browser has to send it.

  Request metrics
  - A line is added to the transcript when each request is sent, with a ticking
    elapsed time and the number of tokens sent, e.g. Waiting for the AI: 2.2 s -
    sent ~10,000 tokens.
  - When the reply arrives it becomes, for example, Received a PTF document in 
    1.2 s - sent 10,234 tokens, received 1,876 tokens, of which 1,210 tokens 
    reasoning. Failed requests show as Request failed after ….
  - It appears for text replies too, since whether a reply is PTF isn't known
    until it arrives. It's easy to limit it to PTF replies if you'd prefer.
  - Token counts: they're taken from the endpoint's usage field, if IFM reports
    one. I couldn't confirm that it does, because I don't have the IFM password.
    Without it, counts are estimated at about 4 characters per token and shown
    with ~ and "(estimated)". The counts never go back to the AI in the
    conversation history.

  Two things for you:
  - demo/tldraw/js/tldraw-credentials.js is tracked by git, although its example
    file says it's gitignored.
  - dist/ and docs/ still need npm run build.

  The new code is mainly demo/tldraw/js/pixabay.js, the reworked
  fluid-demos-imageGenerator.vue, measureCall in fluid-demos-askAnything.vue,
  and the metrics display in fluid-demos-askAnythingEntry.vue.

● The canvas now survives a reload. On load, the tldraw driver restores the
  widgets, their state, any layers redefined on the canvas, and both histories;
  it saves again whenever anything changes. The two undo/redo button groups and
  their shortcuts work. I checked this with real keystrokes across a reload in
  Chromium, and the full suite passes (1428/1428) with lint clean on the files I
  touched.

  Persistence
  - Framework: fluid.persistenceAdapter saves nothing by default.
    fluid.makeLocalStoragePersistenceAdapter() stores one PTF document per page
    URL and ?infusionArenaId value (0 if absent).
  - tldraw driver: switches on the localStorage adapter at startup. The saved
    document is the same material we send the AI as PTF (shapes, plus each
    widget's layers, potentia and live state) together with both history stacks.
  - When it saves: shortly after any canvas or history change, every 5 seconds
    if something else changed, and when the page is hidden. Nothing is written
    until a restore has finished, so a half-restored canvas can't overwrite the
    saved one.
  - Restore: history entries point at widgets by shape id rather than component
    id, so they still work against the rebuilt widgets. The default Hello World
    widget is only created when there's nothing saved.
  - Separate arenas: ?infusionArenaId=other gets its own saved canvas.

  History buttons
  - State ↶ ↷ (Ctrl-Z / Ctrl-Y): steps through changes to the canvas widgets'
    live state. The AI panel's own state is excluded.
  - Layers ↶ ↷ (Ctrl-Shift-Z / Ctrl-Shift-Y): steps through layer redefinitions,
    for example by the AI, including SFC template edits. The layer definitions
    loaded with the page are not included.
  - Tooltips: they show the shortcut, as ⌘Z, ⌘Y, ⇧⌘Z, ⇧⌘Y on macOS (Cmd instead
    of Ctrl) and Ctrl+Shift+Z style elsewhere. Buttons are greyed out when
    there's nothing to step to.

  Things that behave differently, or that you should know
  - tldraw's own Ctrl-Z/Y no longer work from the keyboard. These shortcuts now
    drive our stacks, so tldraw's shape undo is only reachable from its toolbar.
    Shortcuts pressed while typing in a text field are left alone.
  - Every state write is a step. For example, finding an image passes through
    "Finding…" and back, so Ctrl-Z can land on an intermediate state. Writes
    made by pasting, restoring, or the AI changing a widget's state directly
    aren't recorded.
  - More changes are now recorded. I extended the framework so that plain member
    writes on user widgets (e.g. self.timer = …) are recorded, not just writes
    under $reactiveRoot. These also show up in the editor's history pane.
  - Only redefined layers override the page. On reload, a layer redefined on the
    canvas is restored over the page's version; other layers load fresh from
    their files. So your edits to SFC files on disk still appear after a reload.
  - Limits: each stack keeps at most 200 entries. Entries for deleted widgets
    are skipped when stepping. Only the current tldraw page is saved.
    localStorage is capped at roughly 5 MB, and a failed save logs a warning
    rather than failing.
  - Build: dist/ and docs/ still need npm run build for the published demos.

  The new code is mostly the arena section at the end of FluidPTF.js and the new
  demo/tldraw/js/tldraw-arena.js. The rest is shortcut and reference helpers in
  tldraw-hosting.js and the wiring in tldraw-driver.js. The framework hooks are
  fluid.historyListeners and fluid.withoutHistory in Fluid.js.

● The AI's instructions now require fluid.topLevelWidget on every widget it
  synthesizes, and a text search checks each response for it. A response that
  fails is rejected whole and sent back for correction. The full suite passes
  (1440/1440) and lint is clean.

  Ordering: I first intended to have the AI name the layer first in $layers, but
  a quick test showed that breaks. ["fluid.topLevelWidget", 
  "fluid.demos.counter"] fails with an inconsistent hierarchy, because the
  counter already inherits it. ["fluid.demos.counter", "fluid.topLevelWidget"]
  works. So the instructions tell the AI to name it last, even when it's already
  inherited.

  The instructions (in ai-protocol.js): a new bold rule in the response rules
  says any layer the AI defines and builds a widget from must list
  fluid.topLevelWidget as the last of its top-level $layers, with an example for
  a new widget and one adapting the counter. They also tell it that a document
  without it is rejected entirely. The hints on adapting and combining widgets
  now say the same.

  The check (fluid.tldraw.ai.checkTopLevelWidget, run at the end of
  planChanges):
  - When it applies: only when the response builds a new or replacement widget
    from a layer it defines itself, whether at the top level or inside a
    component part.
  - What it looks for: the text fluid.topLevelWidget anywhere in the layers the
    response sends.
  - On failure: nothing from the response is applied, not even its other layers
    or deletions. The AI is told which layers lacked it and asked to resend
    everything. This uses the existing correction loop, so it counts against the
    same attempt limit.
  - Not checked: creating a widget from a layer that already exists, and
    defining a layer without building a widget from it.

  Because it's a plain text search, it would be satisfied by the name appearing
  anywhere in a sent layer, such as a comment or another layer. It also doesn't
  check the order, so a layer that names it first still gets through; that
  widget then fails with the inconsistent-hierarchy problem, which is reported
  back to the AI as before.

  The new tests cover a rejected document, a replacement widget, a layer defined
  inside a component part, the passing and exempt cases, and a two-turn
  exchange where the corrected response is the one applied.

✻ Cooked for 6m 19s · done 14:06

● Background command "Regression scenarios, suite and lint" completed (exit code
0)

  Read 1 file, ran 1 shell command (ctrl+o to expand)

● Undo now works in whole steps rather than individual writes. All 1458 tests
  pass. The only lint complaints are in generated .d.mts files dated yesterday,
  which I didn't touch. I checked the behaviour in Chromium.

  How writes are grouped
  - Rapid writes: writes to the same widget less than 750ms apart become one
    step, so typing a word undoes as a unit.
  - User actions: everything a click or other template event causes is one step,
    until any promise it returns has settled. A search's "Finding…" flag,
    results and flag-off undo together, however slow the network is.
  - No merging across boundaries: a new action always starts a new step, even
    straight after typing. A write after you've undone something never merges
    into the step before it.
  - Scope: grouping is per widget, so activity in two widgets never merges.

  In Chromium I typed "fox", searched, typed " cub", pressed Enter to search
  again, then replaced the text with "owl". Undo stepped back through the owl
  typing, the second search, the " cub" typing, the first search and the "fox"
  typing. Each grouped step also survived a reload.

  Two consequences you should know about
  - Methods triggered by events need to return their promise to be grouped. I
    changed the Image Generator's Enter-key handler to do this, so Enter groups
    like the button. A handler that fires off async work without returning it
    only gets the time-based grouping.
  - Automatic DOM events count as actions too. In my test, Pixabay was
    rate-limiting image loads after my many runs, which fired the widget's
    image-error refresh. That refresh got an undo step of its own that changes
    almost nothing visible. If you'd rather such events stay out of the history,
    error events could be excluded from grouping.

  The main changes are:
  - the grouping itself, in the arena history section of FluidPTF.js
    (pushLiveRecord, withinGesture);
  - FluidView-browser.js, which wraps each template event in a step;
  - FluidSignals.js, which now passes event handlers' return values through so
    their promises reach that wrapper;
  - tldraw-arena.js, which groups by widget and saves grouped steps.

● Your reading was close. The tldraw side wasn't conflicting with the restore;
  the arena had saved the Image Generator mid-search. I've also made the change
  you asked for: widgets are no longer saved as tldraw shapes, only as their
  potentia. I reproduced the problem in Chromium, and after the fix the widget
  restores interactive. All 1458 tests pass and lint is clean.

  Cause: reloading while a search was in flight saved the widget with its
  "searching" flag still set. On restore nothing would ever finish that search,
  so the widget stayed stuck:
  - Dimmed and frozen: a busy widget greys out its input and turns off clicks on
    it, which is the dimming and the lack of interaction you saw.
  - Clicks reaching tldraw: with clicks turned off on the input, they passed
    straight through to tldraw underneath, which is why it seemed to have become
    a plain tldraw shape.

  The fixes:
  - Widgets come back from their potentia alone. The saved tldraw content now
    holds only native tldraw shapes. Each widget is saved as its PTF parts plus
    a small shape part with its layer name and geometry, the same form we send
    the AI. On reload a fresh widget is created with its original id and
    position and rebuilt from those parts. A widget inside a frame goes back
    into the frame.
  - Only settled state is saved. If an action is still running when the arena
    saves (a search awaiting results), the widget is saved as it was before the
    action began. The unfinished undo step is left out of the saved history too,
    so redo can't bring the stuck state back after a reload.

  Checked in Chromium:
  - Reloading mid-search now restores the widget usable, with its query text and
    no "Finding…".
  - A frame holding a counter, a note, and the widgets all come back correctly.
  - Creating, deleting, undoing and redoing across reloads still works.

  Your existing saved arena: it was saved in the old format with the stuck state
  inside it, so it will still load stuck once. It almost certainly also saved
  the half-finished search as its latest undo step. Pressing the Widgets undo
  button (or Ctrl-Z) once should take the widget back to before the search; the
  next save then writes the new format. Failing that, ?infusionArenaId=1 starts
  a fresh arena.

  Copy and paste between canvases still carries widgets inside tldraw's own
  content, unchanged. Only the saved arena moved to potentia alone; I can switch
  copy/paste to the same form if you'd like.

● The metrics line in the "Ask me anything" transcript now leads with uncached
  input tokens, followed by the cached count in brackets. For example: Received 
  a PTF document in 4.2 s - sent 2,234 tokens (8,000 cached), received 1,876 
  tokens, of which 1,210 tokens reasoning. While a request is pending it reads
  Waiting for the AI: 2.2 s - sent ~2,234 tokens (~8,000 cached). All 1466 tests
  pass and lint is clean.

  What counts as cached: the opening of the system prompt that is identical in
  every request, namely the introduction and the framework documentation.
  Everything from the workspace section onwards changes between requests and
  counts as uncached.

  How the number is worked out:
  - Endpoint reports a total: the cached figure is that total multiplied by the
    prefix's share of the request's text, so cached plus uncached always equals
    the reported total.
  - No reported total: the cached figure is estimated at about 4 characters per
    token, and both figures are marked with ~.
  - Endpoint's own cached count: if the endpoint reports one, it's ignored, as
    you said the prefix can be assumed cached.

  The new pieces are fluid.tldraw.ai.cachedTokens in ai-protocol.js, which uses
  the workspace heading to mark where the shared prefix ends, and formatSent in
  the entry SFC.

  The response rules and strategy hints currently come after the workspace, so
  they're paid for in full every time even though they never change. Moving them
  before the workspace would add them to the cached prefix and lower the
  headline figure. I haven't reordered the prompt, since that could affect how
  the model behaves, but it's a small change if you want it.

● The "New shape" dropdown now updates as soon as the AI sends a layer like
  fluid.demos.ai.colourChanger, and each row has a trash can for deleting the
  layer after a confirmation. I checked both in Chromium. All 1500 tests pass,
  lint is clean, and the earlier undo and persistence scenarios still behave.

  Why the AI's layer didn't appear: the dropdown only listed layers from SFC
  files the page had fetched. Layers arriving as text, whether from the AI, a
  paste or a restore, never joined that list, and plain JavaScript layers never
  could. It now lists every defined user layer that has fluid.topLevelWidget
  among its layers, directly or through a parent, and it updates live as layers
  are defined, redefined or deleted.

  The trash cans:
  - A plain <select> can't hold icons, so the dropdown is now a small custom
    list. A red trash can appears at the right of a row when the pointer is over
    that part.
  - Clicking it asks you to confirm, for example: "Delete the layer 
    fluid.demos.ai.colourChanger? The widget on the canvas made from it will be 
    deleted too. The deletion of the layer can be undone with Ctrl+Shift+Z." The
    shortcut is written ⇧⌘Z on Mac. If other layers are built on it, they're
    named as layers that will stop working.
  - Deleting a layer also deletes its widgets. Any widget on the canvas made
    from that layer, or from a layer built on it, is removed too, since it
    couldn't run without it.
  - Undo: Ctrl+Shift+Z brings the layer back and Ctrl+Z brings the widgets back,
    because the two go on the Layers and Widgets stacks respectively.
  - Persistence: a deleted layer that the page itself loads (I tried
    fluid.demos.helloWorld) stays deleted after a reload, and undo still
    restores it.

  Framework bugs found while doing this, all in core code:
  - Deletions weren't recorded in the history. fluid.deleteLayer recorded the
    deletion after removing the layer, at which point the history no longer saw
    it as a user layer, so nothing was recorded. It now records first.
  - A deleted SFC layer couldn't be defined again. Its script and styles stayed
    injected in the page, and re-registering the same text was treated as "no
    change". Deleting a layer now removes its injected script and styles, so
    registering it again re-injects them.
  - A deleted layer coming back went unnoticed by the dropdown. When it was
    redefined, nothing that lists the layers was told a new one had appeared.
    That now counts as a change to the set of layers.

  One other fix: tldraw's style panel was sitting over the right edge of the
  open list, exactly where the trash cans are. The top panel now stacks above
  it.

  Ran 1 shell command (ctrl+o to expand)

● Fixed. All 20 steps of the compose-edit browser script pass again, as do all
  1500 tests and lint on the changed files.

  Cause: a change I made earlier to the framework's history recording.
  Originally only writes inside a component's $reactiveRoot went into the
  history. To make more widget state undoable, I had also started recording
  writes to a component's plain members. The editor relies on the original rule:
  its open tabs are a $reactiveRoot array, but which tab is selected
  (selectedLayerTab) is a plain member, so that history restores tabs without
  restoring the selection.

  Closing a tab removes it from openLayerTabs and then writes selectedLayerTab.
  With my change, that selection write became the newest history entry. So at
  step 16, the back arrow undid the selection rather than the closing, and the
  tab didn't reappear. Each later press was then one step out of phase, which is
  why 17 and 19 passed but 16 and 18 failed.

  Fix: fluid.setForComponent records only writes inside a $reactiveRoot again.
  The one exception is array methods like push and splice, which still always
  record, exactly as before the issue #24 changes.

  Effect on the canvas: a widget's plain members, such as Colin's cat's
  self.timer, are no longer undoable. Every demo widget keeps its state in
  $reactiveRoot, so their undo is unaffected. I re-ran the counter
  create/edit/delete undo scenario across a reload, and it behaves as before.

  Tests:
  - My earlier arena-history tests in FluidPTFTests.js assumed plain-member
    writes were recorded. They now use a second $reactiveRoot instead, and also
    check that a plain-member write isn't recorded.
  - A new FluidILTests.js test copies the editor's tabs-plus-selection pattern
    and checks that back reopens a closed tab and forward closes it again. That
    catches this regression under npm test, so it no longer depends on the
    browser script.
